title: Droplet file
description: One droplet: droplets/<name>.yaml in the infra repo. The source of truth for the droplet's Cloudflare side (SSH route, Private name, site, tunnel routes), who may SSH in or reach its site, its firewall rules (report-only until migration Phase 5) and its OneUptime monitors. The tool writes no DigitalOcean tags (a droplet it creates gets its environment's firewall tag).

name.description: The Droplet name: a lowercase domain in one of the account's zones. Must equal the file name without .yaml.

description.description: Free text: what the droplet is for and who owns it.

profile.description: Droplet profile (profiles/<profile>.yaml). Set it only to have the tool create the droplet; adopted existing droplets have no profile. Create-only: changing it later does nothing to an existing droplet.

env.description: Environment: prod, staging or internal. Picks the region a droplet the tool creates goes to (and the old firewall tag it is created with). Required with a profile; optional otherwise.

frozen.description: Plans show this droplet's changes, but apply skips them, with one exception: its SSH access (its ssh list) is applied, as the ssh-access tag on its existing Cloudflare target and the people on its existing ssh- app. For droplets that need an owner's go-ahead.

ssh.description: SSH access list, a who-list: who may SSH into this droplet, always as ubuntu (root only through the DigitalOcean web console). Groups from account.yaml groups, email addresses in account.yaml email_domain, staff (anyone with a staff login) and token:<name> (a machine caller such as CI: it may reach sshd through the droplet's ssh- route and still logs in with its own key). everyone and ip: are web only.
ssh.x-error: ssh must list at least one entry: every droplet needs someone who can SSH in as ubuntu

monitors.description: OneUptime monitors. Leave out for the default (one HTTP monitor per site hostname when web is set); [] for none.

allOf.x-error: missing required key "ssh": list who may SSH into this droplet as ubuntu (groups from account.yaml groups, emails, staff, token:<name>)

then.x-error: env is required when a profile is set (the region follows the environment)

domain.description: A lowercase domain such as app.example.com.

whoEntry.description: A who-list entry: a group name from account.yaml groups (lowercase letters, digits and dashes, starting with a letter; not staff or everyone), an email address, staff (anyone with a staff login), everyone (no login; web only), token:<name> (a key of cloudflare.service_tokens) or ip:<address or CIDR> (web only).

whoList.x-error: a who-list needs at least one entry, each listed once

path.description: A URL path such as /admin (not /, no query string, no wildcard).

port.description: Port with protocol: 8443/tcp, 5000/udp, or a range 8000-8010/tcp.

cidr.description: IPv4/IPv6 address or CIDR. A bare address means /32 or /128.

tokenName.description: A key of cloudflare.service_tokens in account.yaml.

note.description: Why this access exists (shown in the plan).

web.description: The droplet's site, served through the tunnel (replaces the web-staff/web-public tags and web-config.json).

origin.description: Where the tunnel sends requests; {ip} is the droplet's private IP. Default https://{ip}:443 (certificate not checked).

hostnames.description: Extra one-level hostnames the droplet serves, besides its own name.

access.description: Web access rules: path -> who may reach it. A path covers everything under it (segment by segment: /admin covers /admin/x, not /administrator), the most specific path wins, and "/" is required. "/": [everyone] puts no Access app on the root; everyone elsewhere opens that path; staff, groups and emails need a login; token:<name> is Service Auth; ip:<cidr> is a Bypass for that range. On a site whose "/" is [everyone], paths that need a login answer 404 on the extra hostnames. /healthcheck/: [everyone] (CI's post-deploy check) applies on the droplet's own name only.

propertyNames.x-error: a web.access key must be "/" or a path such as /admin

health_path.description: Path monitors and the cutover pre-flight fetch. Default /healthcheck/ when web.access opens it to everyone, else /.
health_path.x-error: health_path must be "/" or a path such as /healthcheck/

health_accept_app_404.description: Treat the app's own 404 (non-empty body) at health_path as healthy. The tunnel's empty 404 still fails.

hostname.description: One of the site hostnames (the droplet name or web.hostnames).

path.x-error: path must be "/" or a path such as /healthcheck/

allow.description: Who may reach this droplet, grouped by who the caller is. Report-only until migration Phase 5.

droplet.description: Other managed droplets (DigitalOcean firewall rule; private IP in the same region).

tunnel.description: Outside callers through Cloudflare: a tunnel route plus an Access app for who.

ip.description: Fixed outside addresses that can't use Cloudflare (DigitalOcean firewall rule).

swarm.description: Docker Swarm membership. The tool generates the all-pairs swarm rules for the cluster.

encrypted_overlay.description: The overlay network is encrypted (ESP, IP protocol 50). Every member of the cluster must say the same.
